$comment: HAND-AUTHORED — the register of PARKED-WITH-A-TRIPWIRE items (knowledge/_parked.py reads it, never writes it).
Born #269 2026-09-13 on Dave's word: 'store them for future sake, can they be triggered, or can we have a hook so they don't get missed at the appropriate time'.
A row is added when Dave parks something; its status moves to enacted/dropped by hand when he rules. Rows are never deleted — history is data.

Trigger kinds: pack-version-bump (due when _release/_pack_manifest.json version ≠ parked.at_version) · file-changed {path} (due when the path has a commit after parked.at_commit) · event {name} (due when that moment asks: --due <name>).

items.what: SIDEQUEST — LIST vs CARD: when does a list item with columns become a card, or a list-card hybrid? Dave's proposed shape: simple-list · column-list (2 rows x 3 columns) · list-card (stackable in any amount); beyond 3 cols x 2 rows = a stacked card. Research the definitions before any rule; account cards stack like a list (N-account-card note). Rows B-09, B-10 (declined), B-20 (declined), N-account-card.
items.why: Dave 2026-09-14/15 on the harvest sheet: 'we have list items that have 4 or five datapoints, but tehy are stacked in a couple of columns' / 'maybe when we have columns within a list it's actually a card, we need to think about this' / 'lets discuss' / 'beras some research into these definitions'.
items.owner: Dave (the definition); a research lane once he names the shape

items.what: SIDEQUEST — MODAL TAXONOMY: 'modal' covers too many functions. Dave's four containers sharing the lightbox form factor: Lightbox (viewer, maybe carousel, simple actions) · Dialogue (message + one or two buttons) · Modal (a container for most page components, even a mini journey; changes/supplies/spurs the main journey) · Feature launcher (a discrete tool, e.g. a mortgage calculator). Rows R-A-09, R-A-10 (both declined: modals 'shouldn't be used considerately, not sparingly').
items.why: Dave 2026-09-14: 'whats our definition of a modal? for me this sounds like a dialogue' / 'I think we are using the word modal to cover two many functions'. A vocabulary decision first (roles.json / modals.meta), then the rules follow.
items.owner: Dave (the vocabulary); a lane proposes the four metas' when gates once named
